title: Post-digital education
description: We examine education after the digital has become ordinary infrastructure, asking how learning is shaped by platforms, media saturation, maintenance, inequality, and everyday technological habits.

title: Post-digital art education
description: We explore art education in contexts where analog and digital practices are intertwined, attending to studio cultures, image-making, critique, experimentation, and material traces.

title: Post-AI education
description: We study pedagogical life after AI promises by focusing on agency, labor, authorship, assessment, uncertainty, automation, and the cultural imaginaries that surround machine intelligence.

title: Craft, sloyd, and digital materiality
description: We treat craft and sloyd as critical practices for understanding tools, bodies, materials, histories, code, sensors, repair, and the tactile dimensions of digital culture.

title: Sustainable computing and ecological technologies
description: We ask how computing can be studied and practiced through ecological limits, energy use, repair, reuse, slowness, sufficiency, and more careful technological futures.

title: Embodiment and material practices
description: We foreground bodies, senses, gestures, tools, atmospheres, and sites as active participants in research, teaching, learning, and artistic inquiry.

title: Feminist data sciences
description: We engage with feminist approaches to data, classification, visualization, accountability, refusal, situated knowledge, and the power relations embedded in computational systems.

title: Culture, art, and critical technology studies
description: We connect cultural analysis, artistic research, and critical technology studies to understand how technological futures are narrated, contested, designed, and lived.

title: More-than-digital pedagogies
description: We develop pedagogies that move beyond tool-centered thinking toward relational, embodied, ecological, affective, and experimental ways of knowing and making.
